semester: 5th Semester (Winter Semester start); 6th Semester (Summer Semester start)

learning_outcomes.text: Students know, based on concrete examples, the diversity of discontinuous or non-uniform motion processes required in technology.
They can describe these processes verbally and in diagrams with regard to geometric and physical boundary conditions.
They can read and create work diagrams for machines (cyclograms).

They know other machine elements typical for non-continuously rotating movements (e.g., linear guides, linear modules, rolling ball screws, cam followers...) and their selection/design and layout, as well as overarching constructive requirements and solution approaches.
They can kinematically/dynamically animate/simulate simple mechanisms using computer algebra and/or kinematic modules of CAD systems and, if necessary, model them themselves.
They master simple, predominantly illustrative graphical methods of planar kinematic and kinetostatic analysis, as well as individual simple synthesis tasks.

They are aware of the potential superiority of mechanical or combined motion generation over purely electrical concepts for non-uniform and especially for reversing motion specifications, considered from a sustainability perspective (energy consumption).

syllabus_topics: Introduction to technically important motion processes (s, v, a, j – diagrams).
Cyclograms, basic knowledge of motion design.
Linear guide systems, linear modules, rolling ball screws, cam followers, etc.
Constructive peculiarities: Accuracy, adjustment, play: consequences and remedies.
Equivalent mechanisms for planar cam mechanisms.
Simple planar kinematics and kinetostatics (basic equations for four-bar linkages and graphical methods).
Basic syntheses for linkage mechanisms (e.g., dead center construction, general angle assignments).
If applicable, work with Geogebra and/or NX-Kinematics - or use of didactic tools written in these environments.
Fundamental introduction to model concepts for the energy demand of various drive concepts (e.g., inherent movements / tailored drive parameters) and plausibility considerations for them.
If applicable, exemplary treatment of other machine elements, special gearbox designs.
teaching_methods: Exercises with NX Kinematics module and/or Geogebra or tailored didactic tools (if applicable)
assessment_rules: The module examination must be passed. The examination form (written exam or project work) will be announced at the beginning of the lecture.
